docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
📥 immunread — Read immune repertoire data in R

API reference · Issues · ImmunoMind ecosystem

immunread imports AIRR, 10x Genomics, BD Rhapsody, MiXCR, Immcantation, Dandelion, Parse Biosciences, TRUST4, WAT3R, and Adaptive immunoSEQ data into immundata::ImmunData objects. Readers use duckplyr for large datasets and accept manifests through immundata::read_repertoires().

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Install the development packages from GitHub:

install.packages("pak")
pak::pak(c("immunomind/immundata@dev", "immunomind/immunread"))

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
library(immunread)

path <- system.file(
  "extdata", "airr", "2.0-bulk", "contigs.tsv.gz",
  package = "immunread"
)
idata <- read_airr_bulk(
  path,
  schema = c("v_call", "junction_aa"),
  output_folder = tempfile("immunread-")
)

The package is under development; its API may change before version 1.0.

docs.title: Read 10x Genomics V(D)J contigs
docs.text: Source code

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Reads 10x Genomics V(D)J contig annotation CSV files such as filtered_contig_annotations.csv and maps their barcode, locus, gene, sequence, and count fields to AIRR-style columns.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
read_10x(
  path,
  schema,
  manifest = NULL,
  manifest_file_col = "file",
  column_profile = "standard",
  repertoire_schema = "<auto>",
  ...
)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: path One or more repertoire file paths or a file pattern such as “data/\*.tsv”. Use “\” to read the paths from manifest. schema Column names that define receptor identity, such as c(“v_call”, “junction_aa”). Use immundata::make_receptor_schema() to also select one chain or a pair of chains from each cell. manifest An optional data frame with file paths and sample annotations. manifest_file_col The name of the manifest column with file paths when path = “\”. column_profile Which input annotations to keep. “minimal” keeps core identifiers, gene calls, junctions, and counts. “standard” also keeps sequence, region, and alignment annotations. “full” keeps all input annotations after the changes described under Value. Columns required by schema and repertoire_schema are kept with every profile. repertoire_schema Columns that define repertoire groups. This is passed to immundata::read_repertoires(). … Additional arguments passed to immundata::read_repertoires().

docs.title: Value
docs.text:
An immundata::ImmunData object containing the imported 10x contigs. Source columns are copied to the AIRR output column names below when those output columns are not already present. Existing AIRR output column names are kept. The full profile also includes source columns, except where the region and CDR3 fields are renamed or removed as described below.

The reader maps barcode to cell_id, contig_id to sequence_id, and chain to locus. It maps v_gene, d_gene, j_gene, and c_gene to v_call, d_call, j_call, and c_call. It maps cdr3_nt to junction, cdr3 to junction_aa, umis to umi_count, and reads to consensus_count.

For each of fwr1, cdr1, fwr2, cdr2, fwr3, and fwr4, the source name without _aa or _nt contains amino acids. For example, when both source fields are present, fwr1 is copied to fwr1_aa and fwr1_nt is copied to the AIRR output column fwr1. This same pattern applies to all six regions. Source values replace any existing region output fields. If the source name without a suffix is present without a matching _nt field, that name is removed after the amino-acid copy is made. The CDR3 source columns are renamed source_cdr3 and source_cdr3_nt when present. Column names kept unchanged: productive keeps its source name. The reader uses this field to remove unproductive contigs when it is supplied. umi_count records distinct UMIs, and consensus_count records supporting reads. Other source columns keep their names in the full profile. The selected chains in the returned object depend on the schema and count settings passed to immundata.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
library("immunread")

# Use one thread for this small example.
duckplyr::db_exec("SET threads TO 1")

path <- system.file("extdata", "10x", "9.0.1", "contigs.csv.gz",
  package = "immunread", mustWork = TRUE
)
idata <- read_10x(path,
  schema = c("v_call", "junction_aa"),
  output_folder = tempfile("immunread-")
)

docs.title: Read Adaptive immunoSEQ Analyzer and Connector tables
docs.text: Source code

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Reads Adaptive immunoSEQ Analyzer or Connector tables.

Input columns are described in Adaptive’s Analyzer TSV export guide and the legacy Analyzer manual, Sample Export section.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
read_adaptive(
  path,
  schema,
  manifest = NULL,
  manifest_file_col = "file",
  column_profile = "standard",
  repertoire_schema = "<auto>",
  ...
)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: path One or more repertoire file paths or a file pattern such as “data/\*.tsv”. Use “\” to read the paths from manifest. schema Column names that define receptor identity, such as c(“v_call”, “junction_aa”). Use immundata::make_receptor_schema() to also select one chain or a pair of chains from each cell. manifest An optional data frame with file paths and sample annotations. manifest_file_col The name of the manifest column with file paths when path = “\”. column_profile Which input annotations to keep. “minimal” keeps core identifiers, gene calls, junctions, and counts. “standard” also keeps sequence, region, and alignment annotations. “full” keeps all input annotations after the changes described under Value. Columns required by schema and repertoire_schema are kept with every profile. repertoire_schema Columns that define repertoire groups. This is passed to immundata::read_repertoires(). … Additional arguments passed to immundata::read_repertoires().

docs.title: Value
docs.text:
An immundata::ImmunData object containing the imported Adaptive Analyzer or Connector rearrangements. The reader copies source fields to the AIRR output column names below when those output columns are not already present. Existing AIRR output column names are kept. The full profile also includes source columns, except that rearrangement_type is renamed to source_rearrangement_type.

In Analyzer v2 files identified by sequenceStatus, the reader copies vMaxResolved, dMaxResolved, and jMaxResolved to v_call, d_call, and j_call. It copies aminoAcid to junction_aa, nucleotide to sequence, and count (templates/reads) to duplicate_count. The reader sets productive from sequenceStatus == “In”. When frame_type is present, it sets productive from frame_type == “In” instead.

In Analyzer and Connector files without sequenceStatus, the reader copies v_resolved, d_resolved, and j_resolved to v_call, d_call, and j_call. It copies the first available column among cdr3_rearrangement and cdr3_nucleotide to junction, and copies cdr3_amino_acid to junction_aa. It copies the first available column among rearrangement and nucleotide to sequence, and copies templates to duplicate_count.

Column names kept unchanged: productive keeps its name, and rows that are not productive are filtered out. Source seq_reads, sequenceStatus, and frame_type keep their names in the full profile, as do other source fields. The source rearrangement_type describes gene composition and is retained as source_rearrangement_type in the full profile. This is not AIRR’s field for observed, simulated, or inferred origin. Adaptive abundance values are copy counts, not UMI counts, and the reader does not infer UMIs.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
library("immunread")

# Use one thread for this small example.
duckplyr::db_exec("SET threads TO 1")

path <- system.file("extdata", "adaptive", "analyzer", "contigs.tsv.gz",
  package = "immunread", mustWork = TRUE
)
idata <- read_adaptive(path,
  schema = c("v_call", "junction_aa"),
  output_folder = tempfile("immunread-")
)

docs.title: Read an AIRR Rearrangement table as bulk repertoire data
docs.text: Source code

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Reads a bulk AIRR Rearrangement table and keeps productive sequences for repertoire analysis with ‘immundata’.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
read_airr_bulk(
  path,
  schema,
  manifest = NULL,
  manifest_file_col = "file",
  column_profile = "standard",
  repertoire_schema = "<auto>",
  ...
)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: path One or more repertoire file paths or a file pattern such as “data/\*.tsv”. Use “\” to read the paths from manifest. schema Column names that define receptor identity, such as c(“v_call”, “junction_aa”). Use immundata::make_receptor_schema() to also select one chain or a pair of chains from each cell. manifest An optional data frame with file paths and sample annotations. manifest_file_col The name of the manifest column with file paths when path = “\”. column_profile Which input annotations to keep. “minimal” keeps core identifiers, gene calls, junctions, and counts. “standard” also keeps sequence, region, and alignment annotations. “full” keeps all input annotations after the changes described under Value. Columns required by schema and repertoire_schema are kept with every profile. repertoire_schema Columns that define repertoire groups. This is passed to immundata::read_repertoires(). … Additional arguments passed to immundata::read_repertoires().

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
To measure bulk abundance, the function uses duplicate_count when that column is present. It uses umi_count when duplicate_count is absent. When neither column is present, each retained row represents one chain observation without a supplied abundance value.

Count values must be finite whole numbers that are zero or greater. An optional count field can contain missing values, but the selected abundance field must have a value for every productive input row. Missing abundance causes an error and is not replaced with zero or one.

In recognized sequence and count fields, text such as “NA” and “None” becomes a missing value (NA in R). A row is excluded if it has no value for a receptor feature required by schema. These changes do not apply to other source annotations or to metadata added from manifest.

docs.title: Value
docs.text:
An immundata::ImmunData object containing the imported repertoire data. The chain annotations keep the supplied AIRR column names, including v_call, d_call, j_call, junction, and junction_aa when present.

Count column names are kept unchanged. duplicate_count, umi_count, and consensus_count remain separate fields. In AIRR terminology, they describe sequence copies, distinct UMIs, and reads used to build a consensus or contig. Choosing a count field for abundance does not rename the other fields or change their units. The reader also keeps cdr3 and cdr3_aa separate from the junction fields. It does not use one name as a replacement for another.

The available annotations depend on the input and column_profile. ‘immundata’ adds its own analysis columns, and manifest can add sample annotations under their original column names.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
library("immunread")

# Use one thread for this small example.
duckplyr::db_exec("SET threads TO 1")

path <- system.file("extdata", "airr", "2.0-bulk", "contigs.tsv.gz",
  package = "immunread", mustWork = TRUE)
idata <- read_airr_bulk(path, schema = c("v_call", "junction_aa"),
  output_folder = tempfile("immunread-"))

docs.title: Read an AIRR Rearrangement table as single-cell repertoire data
docs.text: Source code

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Reads a single-cell AIRR Rearrangement table and uses its cell identifiers and counts to select receptor chains.

To select chains, the function uses umi_count when it is present. If that column is absent, it uses duplicate_count. If both are absent, it uses consensus_count. Missing values in the selected field cause an error even when another count field has values. The count and missing-value rules described in read_airr_bulk() also apply here.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
read_airr_sc(
  path,
  schema,
  manifest = NULL,
  manifest_file_col = "file",
  column_profile = "standard",
  repertoire_schema = "<auto>",
  ...
)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: path One or more repertoire file paths or a file pattern such as “data/\*.tsv”. Use “\” to read the paths from manifest. schema Column names that define receptor identity, such as c(“v_call”, “junction_aa”). Use immundata::make_receptor_schema() to also select one chain or a pair of chains from each cell. manifest An optional data frame with file paths and sample annotations. manifest_file_col The name of the manifest column with file paths when path = “\”. column_profile Which input annotations to keep. “minimal” keeps core identifiers, gene calls, junctions, and counts. “standard” also keeps sequence, region, and alignment annotations. “full” keeps all input annotations after the changes described under Value. Columns required by schema and repertoire_schema are kept with every profile. repertoire_schema Columns that define repertoire groups. This is passed to immundata::read_repertoires(). … Additional arguments passed to immundata::read_repertoires().

docs.title: Value
docs.text:
An immundata::ImmunData object containing the imported single-cell repertoire data. If cell_id is absent, values from barcode are copied into a new cell_id column. If cell_id is already present, it is used without changing its name. When a source barcode column is supplied, it is also available with column_profile = “full”.

Other AIRR column names are kept unchanged. This includes gene calls, locus, junction, junction_aa, duplicate_count, umi_count, and consensus_count when present. The function does not rename a count field when it uses that field to select chains. These count names describe sequence copies, distinct UMIs, and reads used to build a consensus or contig in AIRR terminology. The reader also keeps cdr3 and cdr3_aa separate from the junction fields.

The available annotations depend on the input and column_profile. ‘immundata’ adds its own analysis columns, and manifest can add sample annotations under their original column names.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
library("immunread")

# Use one thread for this small example.
duckplyr::db_exec("SET threads TO 1")

path <- system.file("extdata", "airr", "2.0-sc", "contigs.tsv.gz",
  package = "immunread", mustWork = TRUE)
schema <- immundata::make_receptor_schema(
  c("v_call", "junction_aa"), chains = "TRB")
idata <- read_airr_sc(path, schema = schema,
  output_folder = tempfile("immunread-"))

docs.title: Read BD Rhapsody AIRR-like contigs
docs.text: Source code

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Reads BD Rhapsody VDJ Contigs AIRR tables and reads their cell, locus, receptor, and count fields into an immundata::ImmunData object.

The reader passes available chains to immundata, which selects chains according to schema and count ranking. It ranks chains by umi_count when present. If that field is absent, it uses duplicate_count. If both fields are absent, it uses consensus_count. Counts used for ranking must be finite whole numbers that are zero or greater, with no missing values.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
read_bd(
  path,
  schema,
  manifest = NULL,
  manifest_file_col = "file",
  column_profile = "standard",
  repertoire_schema = "<auto>",
  ...
)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: path One or more repertoire file paths or a file pattern such as “data/\*.tsv”. Use “\” to read the paths from manifest. schema Column names that define receptor identity, such as c(“v_call”, “junction_aa”). Use immundata::make_receptor_schema() to also select one chain or a pair of chains from each cell. manifest An optional data frame with file paths and sample annotations. manifest_file_col The name of the manifest column with file paths when path = “\”. column_profile Which input annotations to keep. “minimal” keeps core identifiers, gene calls, junctions, and counts. “standard” also keeps sequence, region, and alignment annotations. “full” keeps all input annotations after the changes described under Value. Columns required by schema and repertoire_schema are kept with every profile. repertoire_schema Columns that define repertoire groups. This is passed to immundata::read_repertoires(). … Additional arguments passed to immundata::read_repertoires().

docs.title: Value
docs.text: An immundata::ImmunData object containing the imported repertoires and available annotations. Column names kept unchanged: Supplied AIRR names such as cell_id, locus, v_call, d_call, j_call, junction, junction_aa, and consensus_count keep their names. When umi_count is absent and duplicate_count is present, the source duplicate_count column is renamed to umi_count. Its original value is also kept as source_duplicate_count in the full column profile. When umi_count is already present, duplicate_count keeps its name and its separate copy count. umi_count counts distinct UMIs and consensus_count counts reads supporting consensus sequences. Other available columns depend on the input and column_profile. Source and manifest annotations keep their names.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
library("immunread")

# Use one thread for this small example.
duckplyr::db_exec("SET threads TO 1")

path <- system.file("extdata", "bd", "2.3", "contigs.csv.gz",
  package = "immunread", mustWork = TRUE
)
idata <- read_bd(path,
  schema = c("v_call", "junction_aa"),
  output_folder = tempfile("immunread-")

docs.title: Read Immcantation AIRR-like tables
docs.text: Source code

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Reads Immcantation tables using the AIRR-C format in bulk or single-cell mode and reads their annotations into an immundata::ImmunData object.

In single-cell mode, the reader passes available chains to immundata, which selects chains according to schema and count ranking. In bulk mode, abundance uses duplicate_count when that field is present. If it is absent, abundance uses umi_count. In single-cell mode, chains are ranked by umi_count when present. If it is absent, ranking uses duplicate_count. If both fields are absent, ranking uses consensus_count. Counts used for abundance or ranking must be finite whole numbers that are zero or greater, with no missing values. Unavailable source annotations remain missing and are not reconstructed from other regions.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
read_immcantation(
  path,
  schema,
  manifest = NULL,
  manifest_file_col = "file",
  column_profile = "standard",
  repertoire_schema = "<auto>",
  mode = c("sc", "bulk"),
  ...
)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: path One or more repertoire file paths or a file pattern such as “data/\*.tsv”. Use “\” to read the paths from manifest. schema Column names that define receptor identity, such as c(“v_call”, “junction_aa”). Use immundata::make_receptor_schema() to also select one chain or a pair of chains from each cell. manifest An optional data frame with file paths and sample annotations. manifest_file_col The name of the manifest column with file paths when path = “\”. column_profile Which input annotations to keep. “minimal” keeps core identifiers, gene calls, junctions, and counts. “standard” also keeps sequence, region, and alignment annotations. “full” keeps all input annotations after the changes described under Value. Columns required by schema and repertoire_schema are kept with every profile. repertoire_schema Columns that define repertoire groups. This is passed to immundata::read_repertoires(). mode “sc” for single-cell tables or “bulk” for bulk tables. … Additional arguments passed to immundata::read_repertoires().

docs.title: Value
docs.text: An immundata::ImmunData object containing the imported repertoires and available annotations. Column names kept unchanged: The reader does not convert input column names. AIRR fields kept by the selected column_profile keep their supplied names, including cell_id, locus, v_call, d_call, j_call, junction, junction_aa, duplicate_count, umi_count, and consensus_count. These count columns remain separate. umi_count counts distinct UMIs, duplicate_count counts copies, and consensus_count counts reads supporting consensus sequences. The reader does not treat duplicate_count as a UMI count. Other available columns depend on the input and column_profile. Missing source fields remain absent. Source and manifest annotations keep their names.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
library("immunread")

path <- system.file("extdata", "immcantation", "single-cell.tsv.gz",
  package = "immunread", mustWork = TRUE
)
idata <- read_immcantation(path,
  schema = c("v_call", "junction_aa"),
  mode = "sc", output_folder = tempfile("immunread-")
)

docs.title: Read MiXCR single-cell clones
docs.text: Source code

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Reads MiXCR single-cell clone exports and maps their cell, chain, gene, sequence, and count fields to AIRR-style columns.

The input must have cellGroup, topChains, and uniqueMoleculeCount columns, as in the bundled MiXCR 4.7.0 example. Exported column names depend on the MiXCR version and export options.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
read_mixcr(
  path,
  schema,
  manifest = NULL,
  manifest_file_col = "file",
  column_profile = "standard",
  repertoire_schema = "<auto>",
  ...
)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: path One or more repertoire file paths or a file pattern such as “data/\*.tsv”. Use “\” to read the paths from manifest. schema Column names that define receptor identity, such as c(“v_call”, “junction_aa”). Use immundata::make_receptor_schema() to also select one chain or a pair of chains from each cell. manifest An optional data frame with file paths and sample annotations. manifest_file_col The name of the manifest column with file paths when path = “\”. column_profile Which input annotations to keep. “minimal” keeps core identifiers, gene calls, junctions, and counts. “standard” also keeps sequence, region, and alignment annotations. “full” keeps all input annotations after the changes described under Value. Columns required by schema and repertoire_schema are kept with every profile. repertoire_schema Columns that define repertoire groups. This is passed to immundata::read_repertoires(). … Additional arguments passed to immundata::read_repertoires().

docs.title: Value
docs.text:
An immundata::ImmunData object containing the imported MiXCR single-cell clones. The reader copies source fields to the AIRR output column names below when those output columns are not already present. Existing AIRR output column names are kept. In the full profile, source columns remain alongside the output columns.

cellGroup is copied to cell_id, and topChains is copied to locus. allVHitsWithScore, allDHitsWithScore, and allJHitsWithScore are copied to v_call, d_call, and j_call. Scores in parentheses, such as (123), are removed from the output gene values, including values in existing gene output columns. nSeqCDR3 is copied to junction, and aaSeqCDR3 to junction_aa. uniqueMoleculeCount is copied to umi_count, and readCount to consensus_count. The reader does not copy readCount to duplicate_count or infer that count from reads. Column names kept unchanged: duplicate_count and productive keep their names when present. Rows that are not productive are filtered out when that column is supplied. Other source columns keep their names in the full profile.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
library("immunread")

# Use one thread for this small example.
duckplyr::db_exec("SET threads TO 1")

path <- system.file("extdata", "mixcr", "4.7.0", "contigs.csv.gz",
  package = "immunread", mustWork = TRUE
)
idata <- read_mixcr(path,
  schema = c("v_call", "junction_aa"),
  output_folder = tempfile("immunread-")
)

docs.title: Read Parse Biosciences TCR tables
docs.text: Source code

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Reads Parse Biosciences TCR tables in which each row describes one cell. The reader separates the chains into rows and uses AIRR names for the output annotations.

See Parse’s public immune annotation overview for descriptions of the wide per-cell fields. This reader expects the wide layout with Barcode, TRA_, TRB_, and optional secondary_TRA_ / secondary_TRB_ columns. For AIRR-formatted tcr_annotation_airr.tsv exports, use read_airr_sc().

The reader prepares one row for each supplied primary or secondary TRA or TRB chain. Rows without a CDR3 amino acid sequence are excluded before ‘immundata’ selects the chains used to construct receptors.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
read_parsebio(
  path,
  schema,
  manifest = NULL,
  manifest_file_col = "file",
  column_profile = "standard",
  repertoire_schema = "<auto>",
  ...
)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: path One or more repertoire file paths or a file pattern such as “data/\*.tsv”. Use “\” to read the paths from manifest. schema Column names that define receptor identity, such as c(“v_call”, “junction_aa”). Use immundata::make_receptor_schema() to also select one chain or a pair of chains from each cell. manifest An optional data frame with file paths and sample annotations. manifest_file_col The name of the manifest column with file paths when path = “\”. column_profile Which input annotations to keep. “minimal” keeps core identifiers, gene calls, junctions, and counts. “standard” also keeps sequence, region, and alignment annotations. “full” keeps all input annotations after the changes described under Value. Columns required by schema and repertoire_schema are kept with every profile. repertoire_schema Columns that define repertoire groups. This is passed to immundata::read_repertoires(). … Additional arguments passed to immundata::read_repertoires().

docs.title: Value
docs.text:
An immundata::ImmunData object containing the imported repertoires and available chain annotations. For each of TRA, TRB, secondary_TRA, and secondary_TRB, the reader copies *_V to v_call, *_D to d_call, *_J to j_call, and *_C to c_call. It copies *_cdr3_aa to junction_aa and *_transcript_count to umi_count for chain ranking and *read_count to consensus_count. Barcode maps to cell_id, and the group name supplies locus after removing the secondary prefix. The group name is also recorded in source_chain.

AIRR output columns that are already present keep their names and are used instead of the corresponding source columns. The reader always sets locus and source_chain from the chain group.

If no group has a read-count column, consensus_count is absent. If some groups have that column, chains from groups without it have NA for consensus_count. Missing optional gene calls also have NA.

With column_profile = “full”, original source columns, including Barcode and the wide chain columns, remain under their original names and the mapped columns are added. These source column names are kept unchanged. With column_profile = “minimal” or “standard”, the reader keeps the columns included in that profile. The available columns also depend on the input and schema.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
library("immunread")

# Use one thread for this small example.
duckplyr::db_exec("SET threads TO 1")

docs.title: Read TRUST4 cell tables
docs.text: Source code

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Reads TRUST4 cell tables and separates their chain records into rows with AIRR names for the gene, sequence, and count annotations.

The TRUST4 barcode report format describes the embedded comma-separated chain fields. This reader expects the tabular layout in the bundled example, with X.barcode, chain1, chain2, secondary_chain1, and secondary_chain2 columns. See the TRUST4 paper, doi:10.1038/s41592-021-01142-2.

Each non-empty primary or secondary chain record becomes a row before ‘immundata’ selects the chains used to construct receptors.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
read_trust4(
  path,
  schema,
  manifest = NULL,
  manifest_file_col = "file",
  column_profile = "standard",
  repertoire_schema = "<auto>",
  ...
)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: path One or more repertoire file paths or a file pattern such as “data/\*.tsv”. Use “\” to read the paths from manifest. schema Column names that define receptor identity, such as c(“v_call”, “junction_aa”). Use immundata::make_receptor_schema() to also select one chain or a pair of chains from each cell. manifest An optional data frame with file paths and sample annotations. manifest_file_col The name of the manifest column with file paths when path = “\”. column_profile Which input annotations to keep. “minimal” keeps core identifiers, gene calls, junctions, and counts. “standard” also keeps sequence, region, and alignment annotations. “full” keeps all input annotations after the changes described under Value. Columns required by schema and repertoire_schema are kept with every profile. repertoire_schema Columns that define repertoire groups. This is passed to immundata::read_repertoires(). … Additional arguments passed to immundata::read_repertoires().

docs.title: Value
docs.text:
An immundata::ImmunData object containing the imported repertoires and available chain annotations. The reader splits chain1, chain2, secondary_chain1, and secondary_chain2 at semicolons and makes each record into its own row. Within each record, comma-separated fields 1 through 8 map in order to v_call, d_call, j_call, c_call, junction, junction_aa, source_read_count, and sequence_id. X.barcode maps to cell_id, and the field containing the record is recorded as source_chain. The locus value comes from the first three characters of v_call, or from j_call when v_call is *.

The read-support estimate in field 7 becomes source_read_count. Its fractional part is removed to give consensus_count, matching the upstream AIRR exporter. For example, a read-support estimate of 7.9 gives consensus_count 7. TRUST4 provides no separate UMI count, so consensus_count is used for chain ranking. Empty and * chain fields are skipped. With column_profile = “full”, original input columns such as X.barcode and the embedded chain fields remain under their original names, and the mapped columns are added. These input column names are kept unchanged. source_read_count is also available with this profile. The contents of the chain fields are split into the mapped columns above. With column_profile = “minimal” or “standard”, the reader keeps the columns included in that profile. The available columns also depend on the input and schema.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
library("immunread")

# Use one thread for this small example.
duckplyr::db_exec("SET threads TO 1")

path <- system.file("extdata", "trust4", "1.1.7", "contigs.csv.gz",
  package = "immunread", mustWork = TRUE
)
idata <- read_trust4(path,
  schema = c("v_call", "junction_aa"),
  output_folder = tempfile("immunread-")
)

docs.title: Read WAT3R TCR tables
docs.text: Source code

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Reads WAT3R barcode_results.csv tables in which each row describes one cell. The reader separates the chains into rows and uses AIRR names for the output annotations.

The input contains BC, TRA_, TRB_, and optional TRA.2_* columns. See the WAT3R paper, doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btac382.

The reader prepares one row for each supplied TRA, TRB, or secondary TRA chain. Rows without a CDR3 amino acid sequence are excluded before ‘immundata’ selects the chains used to construct receptors.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
read_wat3r(
  path,
  schema,
  manifest = NULL,
  manifest_file_col = "file",
  column_profile = "standard",
  repertoire_schema = "<auto>",
  ...
)

docs.title: Arguments
docs.text: path One or more repertoire file paths or a file pattern such as “data/\*.tsv”. Use “\” to read the paths from manifest. schema Column names that define receptor identity, such as c(“v_call”, “junction_aa”). Use immundata::make_receptor_schema() to also select one chain or a pair of chains from each cell. manifest An optional data frame with file paths and sample annotations. manifest_file_col The name of the manifest column with file paths when path = “\”. column_profile Which input annotations to keep. “minimal” keeps core identifiers, gene calls, junctions, and counts. “standard” also keeps sequence, region, and alignment annotations. “full” keeps all input annotations after the changes described under Value. Columns required by schema and repertoire_schema are kept with every profile. repertoire_schema Columns that define repertoire groups. This is passed to immundata::read_repertoires(). … Additional arguments passed to immundata::read_repertoires().

docs.title: Value
docs.text:
An immundata::ImmunData object containing the imported repertoires and available chain annotations. Gene column names are converted for each chain group as follows:

  • For TRA, TRAV becomes v_call and TRAJ becomes j_call.
  • For TRB, TRBV becomes v_call, TRBD becomes d_call, and TRBJ becomes j_call.
  • For secondary TRA, TRAV.2 becomes v_call and TRAJ.2 becomes j_call.

The matching TRA_CDR3nuc, TRB_CDR3nuc, and TRA.2_CDR3nuc values map to cdr3. These nucleotide sequences exclude conserved anchor codons. The matching *_CDR3 amino acid sequences map to junction_aa and include the conserved amino acids. WAT3R does not supply a nucleotide junction, so this reader does not create one. The matching *_nReads values map to consensus_count. *_CDR3_UMIcount values map to umi_count for chain ranking. BC maps to cell_id. The chain group supplies locus (TRA.2 is recorded as TRA) and source_chain.

AIRR output columns that are already present keep their names and are used instead of the corresponding source columns. The reader always sets locus and source_chain from the chain group.

If no group has an nReads column, consensus_count is absent. If some groups have that column, chains from groups without it have NA for consensus_count. Missing optional gene calls also have NA.

With column_profile = “full”, original source columns, including BC and the wide chain columns, remain under their original names and the mapped columns are added. These source column names are kept unchanged. With column_profile = “minimal” or “standard”, the reader keeps the columns included in that profile. The available columns also depend on the input and schema.

docs.text:

# Use one thread for this small example.
duckplyr::db_exec("SET threads TO 1")

path <- system.file("extdata", "wat3r", "1.3", "contigs.csv.gz",
  package = "immunread", mustWork = TRUE
)
idata <- read_wat3r(path,
  schema = c("v_call", "junction_aa"),
  output_folder = tempfile("immunread-")
)
